note: Manually-refreshed research digest compiled from public news sources, including regional/vernacular press, local TV channels and YouTube ground reports where available. Not a live news-wire feed — update this file (or re-run research) to refresh. Built for Meesho 3P logistics capacity planning (Delhivery · Shadowfax · Xpressbees): LM/FM manifestation, non-adherence hotspots, and serviceability-loss tracking. Not an official Meesho product.

alerts.title: Manipur: Kangpokpi tense after Sep 20 clash — NH-2 blockade lifted following detainee release, heavy security remains
alerts.summary: Violence erupted in Kangpokpi district on September 20 after a CRPF CoBRA unit arrested six people near Chawangkining/Kholep village. Protesters blocked NH-2 (the Imphal-Dimapur lifeline highway) at Kangpokpi town and Motbung, digging up sections of the road with JCB machines and partially setting a CRPF Casspir armoured vehicle ablaze; unrest spread to Saikul, Sapormeina, Gamgiphai and Taphou. The detained villagers have since been released and the blockade has lifted, but heavy security deployment continues and the underlying arrests-vs-community tension remains unresolved.
alerts.impact: NH-2 is passable again — resume linehaul but keep contingency routing ready given the high risk of fresh flare-ups in Kangpokpi town, Motbung and surrounding Kuki-majority settlements. Continue flagging Kangpokpi district LM/FM as volatile and monitor daily before committing SLA-sensitive shipments.

alerts.title: Himachal Pradesh: 59 roads still blocked as fresh landslide hits Chailchowk-Tattapani road at Kukdiglu, Mandi
alerts.summary: SEOC data shows 59 roads still blocked statewide as of Sep 20-21 — Mandi worst-hit (27), followed by Kullu (12), Kangra (10), Shimla and Una (3 each), and Sirmaur/Lahaul-Spiti (2 each). A fresh landslide at Kukdiglu on the Chailchowk-Tattapani road (Mandi) halted traffic for three hours on Sep 18. Two power transformers and 11 drinking-water schemes remain damaged in Shimla, and IMD has forecast continuing light-to-moderate rain through Sep 21, keeping slope conditions unstable on the NH-3, NH-21, NH-305, NH-505 and NH-707 corridors.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk across Mandi/Kullu/Kangra hill-taluka pincodes — maintain buffer stock at Mandi and Kullu hubs, keep alternate routing ready around Chailchowk-Tattapani/Kukdiglu, and flag feeder-road villages for last-mile delay until slope conditions stabilise past Sep 21.

alerts.title: J&K: Doda-Bhaderwah road still blocked at Chalnai after landslide, no confirmed reopening as of Sep 21
alerts.summary: The Doda-Bhaderwah road remains blocked near Chalnai village after a landslide on September 19 halted vehicular movement between the two towns. Men and machinery have been pressed into debris-clearance, but no subsequent report confirms restoration as of September 21 — the road should be treated as still disrupted.
alerts.impact: Route watch — Doda-Bhaderwah corridor: hold non-essential LM/linehaul via Chalnai until the road is confirmed cleared, and route via alternate approach roads where available for Bhaderwah-side pincodes.

alerts.title: Karnataka: pre-dawn landslide kills five of one family at Montepadavu Kodi, Dakshina Kannada; second death in Belthangady
alerts.summary: Heavy overnight rain triggered a landslide around 4am on September 20 at Montepadavu Kodi in Belthangady taluk, Dakshina Kannada, collapsing a house where six members of the Poojary family were asleep; grandmother Prema Poojary and two grandchildren were killed, with a third child later found dead and others critically injured. Separately, an assistant powerman died while working on an electric pole in Belthangady during the same storm. CM Siddaramaiah has directed the district in-charge minister and Deputy Commissioner to inspect the site; NDRF/SDRF are deployed, and incessant rain continues to affect traffic across the district.
alerts.impact: Serviceability watch — Dakshina Kannada coastal-hill pincodes (Montepadavu and neighbouring hamlets, Belthangady taluk): flag for manual verification before LM attempts given active rescue/relief operations, and build in extra transit buffer on rain-affected approach roads and the NH-66 corridor district-wide.

alerts.title: Kerala: landslide buries plantation shed at Kottakamboor, Vattavada in Idukki's High Ranges, kills two workers
alerts.summary: A rain-triggered landslide on the evening of September 20 buried a garlic-cleaning shed near Kottakamboor, Vattavada in Idukki district's High Ranges, killing plantation workers Balakrishnan and Chinnu (both Kottakamboor natives); Balakrishnan's wife survived with injuries. Days of heavy rain across the border hamlets of Vattavada, Pampadumchola and Kottakamboor have saturated soil, keeping landslide risk elevated.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Idukki High Ranges (Vattavada, Pampadumchola, Kottakamboor): flag these hamlets as high landslide-risk, hold non-essential LM movement on hill roads during active rain spells, and pre-position buffer stock at the Munnar/Idukki hub.

alerts.title: Kerala: Kottapuzha River flash flood sweeps away group near Nilambur, Malappuram — toll rises to 5, one missing
alerts.summary: A sudden surge on the Kottapuzha River near Pookkottumpadam/Ularvattam-TK Colony, Nilambur (Malappuram district) swept away at least six people at an unofficial riverside spot on the evening of September 20, despite no local rainfall — the surge is believed to have come from heavy rain further upstream in forest catchments. The death toll rose to five by September 21 with two more bodies recovered; one person (Sajitha, of TK Colony) remains missing. Victims came from Tirur, Kottakkal, Karuvarakundu and Wandoor.
alerts.impact: Flag Nilambur/Malappuram river-adjacent pincodes and forest-catchment-fed streams for flash-flood risk even absent local rain — hold LM movement near riverside routes during upstream rain spells and verify road conditions before dispatch into the Nilambur taluk.

alerts.title: Bihar: Ganga breaks all-time record at three gauge stations as floods now displace over 4 million across 14 districts
alerts.summary: The Ganga has broken its all-time high-water record simultaneously at three gauge stations, including Gandhi Ghat, Patna at 50.57m — 0.05m above the previous 2016 record. Embankment breaches near Baniya village (Rangra block) and the Brahmottar embankment at Gopalpur, both in Bhagalpur's Naugachia subdivision, have pushed water into Sadhopur, Masudanpur, Baisi, Bhawanipur and neighbouring panchayats. Over 4 million people are now affected across 14 districts including Buxar, Bhojpur, Patna, Vaishali, Samastipur, Munger, Begusarai, Katihar, Bhagalpur and Khagaria; the Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak, Bagmati, Punpun and Ghaghra rivers are also above the danger mark. Nearly 2,000 boats and dozens of SDRF/NDRF teams remain deployed.
alerts.impact: Critical serviceability loss — flag Naugachia subdivision (Baniya, Sadhopur, Masudanpur, Baisi, Bhawanipur, Gopalpur) and other breach-affected panchayats across all 14 districts as non-serviceable until water recedes from record levels. Treat Naugachia as a recurring seasonal non-adherence hotspot and route Bhagalpur/Patna-hub linehaul with heavy buffer; do not commit SLA promises in low-lying diara belts through end of September.

alerts.title: West Bengal: Padma/Ganga erosion spreads to Taranagar (Murshidabad) and Malda's Manikchak, washing away prior anti-erosion embankment
alerts.summary: Padma erosion at Radhakrishnapur (Raghunathganj, Murshidabad) has destroyed over 10 houses and the old Manasa temple, with concern now spreading to Taranagar village (Lalgola PS) where roughly ₹7.5 crore of prior-year anti-erosion embankment work has been half-washed away in a single night — showing existing mitigation infrastructure is failing. In Malda's Manikchak block, fresh Ganga erosion near Shantimor/Gopalpur has claimed roughly 200 metres of riverbank and around 50 houses; all 69 gates of the Indrapuri Barrage have been opened, and officials expect erosion to continue until end-September given fluctuating Ganga levels. ₹3,600 crore has been allotted for anti-erosion works across Malda, Murshidabad and Nadia.
alerts.impact: Serviceability loss — flag Radhakrishnapur, Taranagar (Murshidabad) and Shantimor/Gopalpur/Manikchak (Malda) as non-serviceable as addresses become invalid with active home loss; recommend manual verification calls before LM attempts and route via Malda town/Murshidabad/English Bazar hubs with extra buffer through end-September.

alerts.title: Bay of Bengal depression (not yet named 'Arnab') to approach north AP-south Odisha coast Sep 23; red alert widens to Kalahandi, Rayagada
alerts.summary: IMD's evening bulletin (Sep 20) confirms the system has intensified into a depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal and is forecast to reach only deep-depression strength — not yet a named cyclone — as it tracks toward the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast, arriving around the morning of September 23. Red alert for extremely heavy rain (20cm+) now covers Odisha's Kandhamal, Gajapati, Ganjam and Puri districts on Sep 23, with Kalahandi and Rayagada added for Sep 24; squally winds of 55-65 kmph are expected along the south Odisha-north AP coast Sep 23-24, and 40-50 kmph gusting 60 along the West Bengal-south AP coast. Telangana has 14 districts on high alert (Orange: Mahabubnagar, Nagarkurnool, Nalgonda, Narayanpet) and AP's North Coastal and interior districts (East/West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur, Kurnool, Chittoor, Anantapur and others) are under Yellow alert through Sep 24. Fishermen are advised off the Bay of Bengal in stages through Sep 24.
alerts.impact: Pre-position for Sep 23 landfall — Ganjam/Puri/Gajapati/Kandhamal/Kalahandi/Rayagada (Odisha) and north coastal AP hubs should pre-build 3-4 day buffer stock, suspend fishing-belt LM attempts, and prepare to flag NS for low-lying coastal pincodes from Sep 22. Telangana (Mahabubnagar/Nagarkurnool/Nalgonda/Narayanpet) and AP interior hubs (Kurnool, Anantapur, Guntur, Chittoor belt) should expect waterlogging-linked delays through Sep 24; West Bengal coastal pincodes should also watch for wind-related disruption.

alerts.title: Nagaland: NH-702 partially reopens for light vehicles between Changtongya and Longleng; heavy vehicles still suspended
alerts.summary: The September 11-12 landslide on NH-702 between Changtongya and Longleng (chainage 5+785-6+050) has been partially cleared — light vehicles are now permitted, but heavy-vehicle movement remains suspended since Sep 12 as recurring mudslides amid the ongoing monsoon keep slowing NHIDCL and contractor Nithin Sai Construction's debris-clearance work. The alternate Tangha-Kangching-Merangkong diversion road is also unsuitable for heavy vehicles. Longleng district HQ connectivity remains constrained.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Longleng district: light-parcel LM/FM movement can resume via NH-702 or the Tangha-Kangching-Merangkong diversion, but hold all heavy-vehicle linehaul and keep buffer stock at the Changtongya gateway until full restoration.

alerts.title: Mizoram: Kolasib district landslide risk spreads beyond Vairengte — evacuations at Saihapui 'K', North Chawnpui and Pangbalkawn
alerts.summary: Following the September 12 landslide that killed a 14-year-old boy and injured four in Vairengte town, continuous rain has triggered further precautionary evacuations across Kolasib district: 13 families moved from Saihapui 'K' near the Assam border over Tuichhuahen river flood fears, families in North Chawnpui evacuated amid unconfirmed fears of the Serlui 'B' hydro dam overflowing, a house was destroyed by landslide in Kolasib town, and 3 families were evacuated from Pangbalkawn after landslides left homes structurally unsafe.
alerts.impact: Watch list — Vairengte, Saihapui 'K', North Chawnpui, Kolasib town and Pangbalkawn: flag as landslide/flood-risk during active rain spells, hold non-essential LM movement on hill-slope approach roads and near the Tuichhuahen river, and verify addresses in slide-prone pockets before dispatch.

alerts.title: Punjab: PRTC/PUNBUS/Roadways contract workers announce indefinite chakka jam from September 22
alerts.summary: Contract workers under the Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers Union have announced a complete indefinite chakka jam (road-blockade strike) starting September 22 over demands for regularisation, equal pay and reinstatement, after talks with the state government failed. While primarily a state bus-service strike, chakka jam protests in Punjab have historically spilled into general highway blockades and slowdowns.
alerts.impact: Watch closely from Sep 22 — expect potential highway slowdowns and road-blocking protests across Punjab affecting Delhivery/Shadowfax/Xpressbees linehaul and LM in depot cities (Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Amritsar, Patiala); keep buffer stock and alternate routing ready in case the chakka jam escalates beyond bus depots.

alerts.title: Punjab: Beas, Ravi and Sutlej in spate — 20+ villages evacuated across Fazilka, Gurdaspur, Kapurthala and Hoshiarpur
alerts.summary: Continued upstream rain from Himachal Pradesh has pushed the Beas, Ravi and Sutlej rivers into spate, prompting district administrations in Fazilka, Gurdaspur, Sultanpur Lodhi (Kapurthala) and Mukerian subdivision (Hoshiarpur) to issue evacuation advisories via public-address systems; more than 20 border villages have moved women, children and the elderly to relief camps. NDRF, BSF and the Army have been placed on alert, and Beas floodwater has damaged multiple villages in the Mukerian subdivision.
alerts.impact: Flag Fazilka, Gurdaspur, Sultanpur Lodhi and Mukerian riverside pincodes as at serviceability risk — hold LM attempts in evacuated villages, verify addresses before dispatch, and route Amritsar/Jalandhar-hub linehaul with buffer for border-belt flood pockets.

alerts.title: J&K: NH-44 Jammu-Srinagar highway sees very slow traffic at Ramban-Banihal amid road work and shooting-stone incidents
alerts.summary: Very slow traffic movement was recorded on NH-44 from Sep 18 4pm to Sep 19 4pm due to ongoing road construction/maintenance work between Ramban and Banihal, plus shooting-stone incidents; the Traffic Control Unit Jammu-Srinagar was noted closed at Ramban pending road conditions. NH-44 is the primary highway corridor for goods movement between Jammu and the Kashmir valley.
alerts.impact: Route watch — build extra transit time into First/Last Mile linehaul between Jammu and Srinagar via the Ramban-Banihal stretch; avoid dispatching time-sensitive shipments through this corridor during active TCU closure windows.

alerts.title: J&K: security forces bust LeT logistics module in Rajouri's Chassana; arrests could precede movement restrictions
alerts.summary: Police arrested three people in Rajouri district's Chassana area on September 18 for allegedly harbouring terrorists linked to the 2023 Chassana encounter, recovering a pistol and grenades. While not a direct route disruption, security operations of this kind in the Rajouri-Poonch belt have historically preceded localized mobile-internet suspensions and movement restrictions in J&K border districts.
alerts.impact: Watch item — Rajouri/Poonch border-belt pincodes: monitor for any follow-on movement restrictions or network curbs over the coming days; no current LM/FM action needed but keep contingency routing in mind for this corridor.

alerts.title: Mumbai: heavy-vehicle bans on Vasai-Virar and JVLR corridors for Ganeshotsav immersions through September 25-26
alerts.summary: Mumbai and Vasai-Virar traffic police have banned heavy vehicles from 2pm-midnight on Ganeshotsav immersion days on named routes — Vasai Phata-Dhumal Nagar, Tulinj Bridge-Achole Circle, and the Sativali Naka-Waliv Naka corridor in Vasai East/West, Nalasopara, Naigaon and Madhuban/Tungareshwar — plus a JVLR (Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road) heavy-vehicle closure from 10am Sep 25 to 12pm Sep 26 for the final and largest immersion (Anant Chaturdashi). A no-parking zone is also in force near Saki Naka's L&T Flyover to IIT Market Gate.
alerts.impact: Route restriction — avoid heavy-vehicle linehaul on JVLR and the named Vasai-Virar corridors during the stated windows through Sep 26; reroute Mumbai-suburb LM/FM via alternate roads and expect delays around immersion sites through Anant Chaturdashi (Sep 25).

alerts.title: Gujarat: Ahmedabad underpasses waterlogged after Vasna Barrage release raises Sabarmati backflow
alerts.summary: IMD flagged widespread thunderstorm activity across Gujarat on September 19; a fresh release at the Vasna Barrage raised Sabarmati river levels and worsened drainage backflow in west Ahmedabad, flooding named underpasses at Akhbarnagar, Mithakhali, Stadium, Usmanpura and Makarba, with BRTS corridors at Hanumanpura, Juna Vadaj and Science City also affected. AMTS/BRTS/GSRTC route diversions remain in force, and north Gujarat districts (Aravalli, Sabarkantha, Banaskantha, Dahod, Chhota Udepur) saw related heavy rain.
alerts.impact: Route watch — avoid the named Ahmedabad underpasses during active rain/release windows; expect LM delays on the Ahmedabad-Vadodara corridor and build buffer time for deliveries routed through west-Ahmedabad BRTS corridors.

alerts.title: Maharashtra-Gujarat: yellow alerts for Nashik/Marathwada and flash-flood watch in Saurashtra-Kutch as monsoon withdrawal begins
alerts.summary: IMD issued yellow alerts for thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds across Nashik, Nashik Ghatmatha, Ahilyanagar and the Marathwada belt (Beed, Parbhani, Hingoli, Dharashiv, Latur, Nanded) on Sep 20, with a broader forecast of a significant rainfall increase across Maharashtra and Goa through Sep 25. Saurashtra-Kutch (Rajkot, Jamnagar, Porbandar, Junagadh, Morbi, Devbhumi Dwarka, Kutch) remains under a flash-flood watch issued Sep 15 for isolated heavy rain and 30-50kmph gusts in coastal/low-lying belts, even as IMD notes conditions are turning favourable for monsoon withdrawal from West Rajasthan, Punjab and Saurashtra-Kutch over the next 2-3 days.
alerts.impact: Keep contingency buffer for Nashik/Marathwada FM lanes and Saurashtra-Kutch coastal/low-lying pincodes through Sep 25; downgrade this watch once monsoon withdrawal is confirmed over the region.

alerts.title: Karnataka: Agumbe Ghat heavy-vehicle ban stays in force through September 30 on landslide risk
alerts.summary: IMD continues to flag thunderstorm and lightning risk over Kodagu, Chikkamagaluru and Shivamogga; the monsoon-season ban on heavy vehicles on the Agumbe Ghat road remains in force until September 30 due to landslide risk, forcing staggered convoys and hairpin-bend delays even for smaller vehicles on this Western Ghats corridor.
alerts.impact: Standing routing constraint — avoid heavy-vehicle linehaul on Agumbe Ghat through Sep 30; plan staggered/smaller-vehicle movement or alternate ghat routes for the Shivamogga-Udupi corridor FM/LM until the ban lifts.

alerts.title: Sikkim: NH-10 landslide at Bardang (20th Mile) disrupts Sikkim-Siliguri lifeline; multiple district roads also blocked
alerts.summary: Heavy rain over Sep 17-18 triggered a major landslide at Bardang (20th Mile) on NH-10, the sole highway artery connecting Sikkim to Siliguri and the plains. Secondary roads are also blocked across Gangtok, Pakyong, Mangan, Namchi, Gyalshing and Soreng districts, including the Singtam road at Aapdara/Marchak, the Dikchu-Mangan road at Zin Khola, and the Darap-Rimbi-Yuksam road (closed since Sep 14). Some stretches are regulated via single-lane diversions.
alerts.impact: Critical route watch — NH-10 is Sikkim's only major supply corridor; hold non-essential linehaul through Bardang/20th Mile, pre-position buffer stock at the Siliguri gateway, and flag Gyalshing/Soreng/Namchi hill pincodes for LM delay until secondary roads clear.

alerts.title: Arunachal Pradesh: landslides block Zemithang-Tawang and Balipara-Chariduar-Tawang roads, stranding vehicles at the China border belt
alerts.summary: A landslide near Shakti village has cut the Zemithang-Tawang road in Tawang district, while a separate landslide near Kaspi/Nag Mandir has blocked the strategic Balipara-Chariduar-Tawang road in West Kameng district, stranding dozens of vehicles on both sides. These are the primary supply corridors connecting Tawang and West Kameng's border settlements to Sonitpur, Assam.
alerts.impact: Serviceability risk — Tawang and West Kameng border pincodes have limited alternate routing; expect extended LM/FM delays and hold heavy shipments until NHIDCL clears both stretches.

alerts.title: Assam: Brahmaputra erosion intensifies at Majuli's Aphalamukh and Chabua, threatening farmland and village roads
alerts.summary: Strong Brahmaputra currents have caused severe embankment erosion in Majuli Island's Aphalamukh area since late August, threatening farmland, tea gardens and homes across Majuli and Chabua. This is a slower-burn, chronic erosion pattern rather than a sudden event, but remains an active threat to riverine village infrastructure and local access roads.
alerts.impact: Background watch — flag Majuli Island and Chabua riverside pincodes for gradual road/address instability; verify access routes periodically as erosion progresses through the post-monsoon period.

alerts.title: Nationwide: Samyukta Kisan Morcha calls Bharat Bandh for September 27, NH1 Delhi-Haryana-Punjab blockades expected
alerts.summary: The Samyukta Kisan Morcha has called a Bharat Bandh for September 27, with farmer groups expected to stage highway blockades along NH1 through Delhi, Haryana and Punjab as in previous rounds of farmer protest action.
alerts.impact: Pre-plan for Sep 27 — expect linehaul delays on the Delhi-Haryana-Punjab NH1 corridor and possible spillover route blockades; advance-dispatch time-sensitive shipments before Sep 26 and prepare SLA-relaxation messaging for affected pincodes.

alerts.title: Petrol/diesel unchanged Sep 21 (Delhi ₹101.96/₹95.44) as Brent eases to ~$101.7 on Saudi Hormuz-route export ramp-up
alerts.summary: Retail fuel prices remain unchanged for a second straight day — Delhi petrol ₹101.96/litre, diesel ₹95.44/litre — with commercial 19kg LPG steady at ₹2,747.50 and domestic 14.2kg LPG at ₹942, following Sep 1's second-straight-month hike. Crude has eased slightly (Brent ~$101.7/bbl, WTI ~$98.2/bbl) as Saudi Arabia ramps Hormuz-route exports above 4 million bpd to offset the ongoing Iran-conflict disruption risk to the Strait of Hormuz, which remains a live geopolitical risk factor.
alerts.impact: Cost watch, no action yet — no immediate LM/FM disruption; continue tracking daily given the Strait of Hormuz remains a live risk. A renewed spike toward $105+ would raise the chance of a fuel-surcharge ask from Delhivery/Shadowfax/Xpressbees — flag early to network-cost teams if crude trends back up.
